features.text: The patient injured his right shoulder a few days ago while playing tackle football.
The injury occurred when the patient was tackled and landed on his shoulder.
The patient experiences pain in the right shoulder when lifting it to the ear.
The patient has difficulty lifting heavy objects with the right shoulder.
The patient experiences consistent pain in the right shoulder since the injury.
The patient has difficulty reaching down to pick up heavy objects with the right arm.
The patient can still perform daily activities like dressing and grabbing a cup of coffee.
The patient experiences tenderness on the back of the right shoulder near the collarbone area.
The patient does not recall any swelling or bruising in the right shoulder area.
The patient does not notice any popping or clicking sensations during movement of the right shoulder.
The patient has not experienced numbness or tingling in the fingers, arm, or hand since the injury.
The patient has not experienced weakness in the right arm or difficulty with fine motor skills like buttoning a shirt or writing.
The patient has not had any prior imaging studies or evaluations of the right shoulder following the injury.
The patient is willing to undergo imaging studies such as a CAT scan to evaluate the right shoulder injury.
The patient can lift the right arm to about shoulder height but experiences pain when attempting to raise it higher or move it around too much.
The patient experiences discomfort when rotating the right arm outward.
